subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After the in-flight persistence race is fixed, should deferred turn maintenance permanently use this new disabled-by-default millisecond setting and generic queue timeout hook, or reuse the existing compaction timeout/abort policy?
rationale: Correctness can be repaired mechanically, but source evidence cannot determine which public operator setting and shared queue API maintainers want to support long term.

options.title: Adopt the opt-in maintenance timeout
options.body: Keep the dedicated disabled-by-default setting and queue hook after the persistence lifecycle is made safe and focused upgrade tests pass.

options.title: Reuse compaction timeout policy
options.body: Replace the new setting with the existing compaction safety budget while retaining the same late-side-effect fencing and persistence ownership.

options.title: Retain unbounded maintenance
options.body: Decline the new contract and accept reliance on the longer session-level abort for wedged background maintenance.

recommendation.title: Adopt the opt-in maintenance timeout
recommendation.body: Keep the dedicated disabled-by-default setting and queue hook after the persistence lifecycle is made safe and focused upgrade tests pass.

likelyOwner.reason: The history ties this person to merging and shaping the original context-engine background-maintenance and task-routing contract.
